heard: A postage stamp declaring Pluto unexplored inspired a spacecraft to visit it. In 1991, the Postal Service released stamps showing every planet alongside its visitor, except the ninth. The Pluto stamp simply read Pluto, not yet explored. The phrase irked scientists, so much it became a call to arms for a new mission. On January 19, 2006, New Horizons launched as the fastest object ever sent from Earth. A Jupiter gravity assist shaved three years off the voyage, sending the probe speeding toward the outer solar system. On July 14, 2015, the spacecraft finally completed its historic close flyby of Pluto. Hidden on board was that exact 1991 stamp, finally delivered to its destination. A postage stamp declaring Pluto unexplored inspired a spacecraft to visit it.
